Welcome to the Birb Cube Wiki

This is the guide to Birb Cube, a holographic bird garden on a table in a spaceship cabin. You scatter seed, birds come, and you get to know them: who comes back, who is bold, who naps on the rock.

New here? Read First steps first, then Controls.

Did you know...

  • ...that every bird in a new world arrives because of seed? Nothing lives in the garden until something draws it in. See Birds.
  • ...that a Frostcrest is drawn only by Blue Barley until you have seen one? See Frostcrest.
  • ...that a bird eating its favorite seed shows a little heart over its head? See Birds and your seed.
  • ...that seed in a feeder stays fresh, while seed on the ground spoils, faster in the rain? See Seed.
  • ...that regulars learn where you feed them, and fly straight back there? See Feeding spots.
  • ...that the Hawk's Shadow is the only danger in the garden, and nobody gets hurt? See The Hawk's Shadow.
  • ...that a rainbow shows only when the sun is low and rain is still falling opposite it? See Rainbows.
  • ...that Night Owls keep the opposite hours, and Dusk Doves are the night crowd? See Day and night.

Birb Cube

From the Birb Cube Wiki, in Getting started
Birb Cube
The cabin, the cube and the side columns
Information
TypeHolographic bird terrarium
MakerA company that loves the Middle Ages
InsideA patch of a living bird world

Birb Cube is a toy on a table in a cabin aboard a spaceship. A glowing cube floats over the Halo Puck, and inside it is a patch of a bird world: grass, rocks, a pond, a creek and birds.

The cube shows only part of a bigger land. Birds come and go through the fog at its walls. You can move the view around, step inside it, and switch the cube to a seed store, the The Gilded Granary.

Its maker loves the Middle Ages, which is why the birds are called Emberwings and Gildfinches, the store is a granary and you pay in feathers.

What you do

  • Scatter seed and fill feeders, so birds come and stay. See Feeding.
  • Watch and get to know them: each bird has a name, a few Traits and a favorite seed.
  • Pick up the feathers they drop and spend them on seed and feeders. See Feathers.
  • Design your own birds in the The Birb Designer.

The cozy rule

Nothing in Birb Cube punishes you. Birds never die of neglect: a hungry bird leaves, and may come back. Time passes only while the game is running. Paying attention gets you more, but looking away costs nothing.

First steps

From the Birb Cube Wiki, in Getting started
First steps
Information
TimeA few minutes
For every key and click, see Controls.
Contents
  1. Switch it on
  2. Scatter some seed
  3. Wait for birds
  4. Pick up feathers
  5. Visit the store

Switch it on

The box starts off. Click the red power button with the Birb Cube logo on the control deck in front of the cube.

Scatter some seed

Click a seed bag in the left column to put a scoop in the seed bucket. Then hold the right mouse button over the garden to pour where the bucket hangs. A tap pours a pinch; holding pours more. See Pouring.

A new world already has a little wild seed lying about, so the first birds may arrive before you pour anything.

Wait for birds

Birds fly in through the fog to seed they like. A line over each new bird's head says it "has entered the chat". Click a bird to see its bird card.

Pick up feathers

A bird that finishes a good meal sometimes drops a feather. Click it before it fades. Feathers are the money of the The Gilded Granary, where you buy more seed and feeders.

Visit the store

Flip the BIRB / SHOP rocker on the control deck to SHOP to show the store in the cube. More shelves open as you collect new kinds of feathers. Flip back to BIRB to return.

  • Pouring

The Hologram View

From the Birb Cube Wiki, in Getting started
The Hologram View
Standing in the garden at noon
Information
EnterDouble-click the cube
LeaveDouble-click again

Double-click the cube while it shows the birds to step inside. You stand low in the garden and look across it at bird height.

Inside, the garden carries on past the cube's walls into mist and a treeline. The cabin is replaced by a sky, with the sun, moon and stars where they should be for the time of day. Birds and rain sound louder, and you hear the forest by day.

  • Drag sideways to turn, up and down to look lower or higher.
  • The mouse wheel zooms the bird world.
  • The side columns slide away; move the mouse to a screen edge to bring them back.
  • The cabin's controls don't work from inside. Double-click again to come back out.

Some things show only from inside: Rainbows, far lightning over the treeline in a thunderstorm, and the land beyond the walls.

The Hologram View is for the birds only, not the store.

The Esc menu

From the Birb Cube Wiki, in Getting started
The Esc menu
Information
OpenEsc

Esc opens the menu and pauses the garden; closing it puts things back as they were.

  • Resume: back to the game.
  • Birb Designer: see The Birb Designer.
  • Wiki: opens this wiki in your browser.
  • Fullscreen or Windowed.
  • Settings: volumes (master, the hologram's hum, birds, effects), hand color (a strip of shades, or Groening yellow), fullscreen type, name tags (birds you named, all birds, or off), hologram quality (high, medium, low), lightning glow (soft, faint, off), and what stands on the table beside the cube: the The radio or the TV.
  • Controls: the list of keys and clicks.
  • New world: starts over with fresh ground, a new pond and creek, and no birds. It asks first. Your settings stay.
  • Quit: asks first, then saves and closes.

Saving and time away

From the Birb Cube Wiki, in Getting started
Saving and time away
Information
SavesEvery couple of minutes and on quit
While closedTime stands still

The garden saves every couple of minutes and when you quit: the birds, the regulars who are away, the seed, your feathers, the weather and the time of day. Settings are saved separately, so a New world keeps them.

Time does not pass while the game is closed; you come back to the hour you left. While the game is running, the birds keep living even with the box switched off or the store showing.

The cabin

From the Birb Cube Wiki, in The cabin
The cabin
The table, the cube and the window behind
Information
PlaceA small cabin on a spaceship

You sit at a table in a small cabin on a spaceship, with a window onto the stars behind it. On the table are Birb Cube, the The radio or the TV, and a few odds and ends.

Day, night, rain and storms happen only inside the cube; the cabin stays the same.

Your hands

Two hands appear when there is something to do and fade away after: they press buttons, turn knobs and hold the compass ring while you turn the cube. Set their color in the Esc menu's Settings: blue-green shades, or Groening yellow.

From the Birb Cube Wiki, in The cabin
The Halo Puck
Information
Made ofWalnut and brass
CarriesThe cube and the compass ring

The Halo Puck is the base the cube floats over.

The compass ring around the cube turns with it when you drag. Its letters (N, E, S, W) show which way the garden faces. The build's name is engraved on it.

The control deck

From the Birb Cube Wiki, in The cabin
The control deck
The deck sits in front of the cube
Information
ControlsPower button, BIRB / SHOP rocker, day dial

The control deck is the console on the table in front of the cube. Left to right:

  • The power button: the red button with the Birb Cube logo. Switches the cube on or off.
  • The BIRB / SHOP rocker: switches the cube between the garden and the The Gilded Granary. The lit half shows which one is up. It only works while the box is fully on.
  • The day dial: the time of day in the garden. Night is blue, dawn rose, day gold and dusk amber; the sun marks noon and the moon midnight.

The radio

From the Birb Cube Wiki, in The cabin
The radio
Information
PlaysYour music and web radio
DialFM, 88 to 108

The radio beside the cube plays two kinds of station.

  • Folder stations: each sub-folder of the Radio folder next to the game is a station playing your own songs. Stations keep playing while you are tuned away, so you tune in partway through a song. A station.txt inside can set its name and frequency.
  • Web stations: live internet radio. Click the radio's tuning window to open the station finder, where you search by name, genre or country (or paste a link), listen, and add stations to your dial.

Drag the knobs or use the wheel over them. Between stations you hear static. The radio plays quieter while the Esc menu is open and inside the The Hologram View.

The TV

From the Birb Cube Wiki, in The cabin
The TV
Information
PlaysPublic-domain shows and your videos
SwapEsc menu, Settings, On the table

The TV can stand in the radio's place (choose it in the Esc menu's Settings). It has power, volume and channel buttons; the wheel over it sets the volume.

Each channel is set in TV/channels.txt next to the game: a public-domain collection from the Internet Archive, or a folder of your own videos. Channels keep playing while you are away from them. Empty channels show static.

The side columns

From the Birb Cube Wiki, in The cabin
The side columns
The right column with a bird's card
Information
LeftThe seed bucket, ATTRACTS
RightThe garden's stats, the bird card, the map

There is a column on each side of the screen.

Left column

The seed bucket: the seed bags, Stir and Empty, the bucket itself, the label of the bag under your mouse, and ATTRACTS, which species the seed in the bucket would draw.

Right column

The garden's stats: how many birds and how much food are about, the time of day ("Day 3, Spring" and a dial), the Weather word, and your feather collection: a colored dot and a count for each kind you have found. Hover a dot for its name.

Under the stats, the card of the selected bird or feeder, and the map of the world: click or drag it to move the view, and use its + and - to zoom. In the store the map becomes the Zoo Cam, a live view of the garden; click it to go back.

The garden

From the Birb Cube Wiki, in The garden
The garden
The garden from inside
Information
SizeFar bigger than the cube shows
EdgesFog

The garden is a patch of rolling land with grass, bare dirt, a few rocks, a pond called the Wellspring and a The creek. Each new world makes a new one.

The cube shows only part of it. Pan with W, A, S, D or the map, and zoom with the wheel. You can't pan past the fog at the edges; birds come and go through it.

Birds walk the slopes, seed rolls a little way downhill, and rain collects in the hollows.

WearsWhere birds feed

Rocks

From the Birb Cube Wiki, in The garden
Rocks
Information
Per worldA few big ones and several small

Each world has a few big rocks and some small ones. Birds walk around them and now and then hop up and sit for a while. Bold birds take the high rocks; a Watchman climbs up and keeps watch long after the others have left. Some birds sleep on a rock at night or for a nap.

Seed that lands on a rock rolls off it.

The Wellspring

From the Birb Cube Wiki, in The garden
The Wellspring
The Wellspring, the pond of the garden
Information
Per worldOne
Used forDrinking and bathing

The Wellspring is the garden's pond.

Birds come to drink, or wade in to bathe and shake off after. Only a few bathe at once. A thirsty bird goes to the nearest water, and flies if it is far. A Dabbler wades into any water it passes.

Seed that lands in the water sinks. Feathers that fall in wash up on the shore. Feeders can't be set down in it.

The creek

From the Birb Cube Wiki, in The garden
The creek
Information
Per worldOne
RunsThrough the whole land

The creek runs in from the fog at one edge of the world, through the Wellspring, and out past the far edge. You hear it when the view is near.

Birds hop across the narrow stretches and fly over the wide ones. They drink and bathe at its shallow edges too. Seed that lands in it drifts downstream and sinks. It rises a little after rain and goes back down as the ground dries.

From the Birb Cube Wiki, in The garden
Puddles
Information
AppearIn the rain
Used forDrinking only

While it rains, a few puddles form in the hollows. They dry up after. Birds drink from them but don't bathe in them; a thirsty bird uses one if it is nearer than the pond.

Sprouts

From the Birb Cube Wiki, in The garden
Sprouts
Information
Grow fromSeed that rotted
LastAbout a quarter of an hour

A heap of seed that rots away sometimes comes up as a grassy tuft. It grows seedheads of the same seed, birds peck at them, it drops a little seed of its own, then dies back. Uneaten seed is never wasted, and never leaves a mess to clean up.

Day and night

From the Birb Cube Wiki, in Time and weather
Day and night
Dusk from inside the garden
Information
Day lengthAbout a quarter of an hour at normal speed
Shown onThe day dial and the right column

A full day and night takes about a quarter of an hour at normal speed. The day dial and the right column show the time. Only the garden has day and night; the cabin stays the same.

At night birds glow a little brighter, so you can still see and click them.

What birds do

  • Birds sing most at dawn and less in the evening.
  • At night most birds fly off to roost and come back in the morning. A few sleep in the garden, on a rock or the ground, with z's over them.
  • Birds nap now and then, usually in the afternoon.
  • Night Owls are awake at night. They wake a little before sunset and sleep soon after sunrise. Many Dusk Doves are Night Owls.
  • Early Risers wake before dawn and go to roost earlier than the others.

Seasons

From the Birb Cube Wiki, in Time and weather
Seasons
Sunrise in spring, from inside the garden
Information
OrderSpring, Summer, Autumn, Winter
LengthFive days each

The year has four seasons of five days each. The right column shows the day and season, for example "Day 3, Spring". Days are longer in summer and shorter in winter.

Seasons also change the Weather: dry spells are shorter in spring and longer in summer, and thunderstorms come mostly in summer.

Weather

From the Birb Cube Wiki, in Time and weather
Weather
A downpour from inside the garden
Information
ShownThe word under the time, right column

Dry spells and rain spells come and go. The word under the time in the right column says what the weather is doing. Rain forms Puddles and darkens the ground, which dries over a few hours.

The weather words

WordMeans
Fair skiesClear
GatheringClouds coming in, rain on the way
MizzlingA light drizzle
ShowersSteady rain
DownpourHeavy rain
ThunderstormA storm, see Thunderstorms
MendingThe rain is over and the sky is clearing

Birds in the rain

Birds hunch up, call less and leave sooner, and fewer arrive. Nobody bathes in the rain. Rain-proud birds don't mind it, so many of the birds that arrive in the rain are Rain-proud.

Rain spoils seed on the ground faster. Seed in feeders and on sprouts' seedheads stays fresh, so feeders matter most in wet weather.

Thunderstorms

From the Birb Cube Wiki, in Time and weather
Thunderstorms
Information
SeasonMostly summer
DangerNone

A thunderstorm is a heavier rain spell that builds over about an hour, with thunder getting closer. Lightning lights up the clouds rather than flashing; the Esc menu's Settings can soften it or turn it off. From inside the The Hologram View, you sometimes see bolts far off over the treeline.

Close thunder startles birds by their nerve, a little like the The Hawk's Shadow: Faint-hearted birds scatter, others freeze. Rain-proud birds are less jumpy. Almost no birds arrive in a storm except Rain-proud ones.

  • The Hawk's Shadow

Rainbows

From the Birb Cube Wiki, in Time and weather
Rainbows
Information
Seen fromThe Hologram View only

A rainbow shows when the sun is up but low and rain is still falling on the opposite side of the sky. That mostly happens when rain clears early or late in the day. Sometimes a fainter second bow shows outside the first.

You can only see it from inside the garden, in the The Hologram View; from the room there is no sky. A line in the log tells you when one is up.

Birds

From the Birb Cube Wiki, in Birds
Birds
Birds settling in the garden
Information
ArriveDrawn by seed they like
LeaveFull, bored, hungry, or old

Every bird in the garden came because of seed. A new world starts with no birds and a little wild seed. Birds fly in through the fog to seed they like, and more seed draws more birds. Seed in a feeder draws them better than seed on the ground.

A bird's day

Each bird has a home patch, where it last finished a meal. It stays near home: eating, drinking, napping, calling, preening and sitting on rocks. It turns back before the edge of the world, and keeps living when it is outside the cube's view.

Leaving

  • Now and then a bird loses interest and flies off, much sooner when there is nothing it likes to eat.
  • A need left at nothing for too long sends it off, though water is always near and a nap can be taken anywhere, so that is rare.
  • Birds grow old and leave for good after a few hours of game time.

A bird that leaves for any reason but old age may come back later as a regular. A bird that leaves says so over its head ("has left the chat").

Needs

From the Birb Cube Wiki, in Birds
Needs
Information
NeedsFood, water, rest
ShownBars on the bird card

Each bird has three needs that run down over time: Food, Water and Rest. When one runs low the bird sees to it, the most pressing first: it looks for food it likes, goes to the nearest water to drink or bathe, or takes a nap. A night's roost fills Rest too.

The bird card shows the three bars and what the bird is doing right now.

Traits

From the Birb Cube Wiki, in Birds
Traits
Traits on the bird card; hover one for its line
Information
Per birdTwo or three
ChangeNever

Every bird gets two or three traits when it first arrives, and keeps them for life (a regular brings them back). Each trait sits on a scale, like Nerve or Appetite, and a bird holds at most one trait on each scale. On every other scale it is average.

Traits change what a bird does: how close it gets to others, how much it eats, how far it roams, how often it calls, when it sleeps, whether rain bothers it, how often it comes back, how freely it drops feathers. Each Species leans a certain way: Emberwings are often Stout-hearted, Dusk Doves often Night Owls.

The bird card shows the traits a bird has; hold Left Alt to see every scale. Hover a trait for its line and what it changes.

Every trait

ScaleTraitWhat it is like
NerveFaint-heartedStartles at its own shadow. Keeps well clear of other birds, eats where no one else is, and only sits on an empty rock.
NerveWaryTrusts its own kind and few others. Keeps a little room around itself, and would rather not eat beside a stranger.
NerveStout-heartedFears nothing smaller than a hawk. Shoulders in close and claims the high rocks.
AppetiteDaintyTakes its seed one grain at a time, and is full before the others have begun.
AppetiteBig EaterEats as if the granary closes at dusk. Hungry often, gobbles fast, and roams far for a meal.
RoamingHearthboundKeeps to its own patch of grass, rarely tires of it, and nearly always comes home.
RoamingWayfarerRanges wide, tires of a place quickly, and may never pass this way again.
VoiceHushedSpeaks seldom, and never over another bird.
VoiceTown CrierHas news for everyone, often, and will not wait its turn.
HoursEarly RiserUp before the first glow and singing about it. Tires early, and is off to roost while the others are still at supper.
HoursNight OwlKeeps lantern hours. Sleeps the day away, and wanders the dark garden long after the rest have gone to roost.
WeatherRain-proudTakes a downpour as a compliment. Stays out in it, eats, and sings while the others huddle.
BathingDabblerNever passes water without wading in. Bathes long and often, and comes out looking pleased with itself.
PerchingWatchmanClimbs to the high rock and keeps watch from it, long after the others have gone back to the grass.
TasteParticularKnows exactly what it likes. Passes over every other pile while its favorite is about, and settles for less only when truly hungry.
LoyaltyOath-keeperGave the garden its word, and keeps it. Whenever it flies off, it is the first to come back.
GivingOpen-handedNever leaves a table without leaving something behind. Drops its feathers more freely than most.

The first five scales have two or three traits each. The last six have a single, rarer trait. An Oath-keeper is never a Wayfarer.

The bird card

From the Birb Cube Wiki, in Birds
The bird card
A selected bird's card, right column
Information
OpenClick a bird

Click a bird to select it. Its card appears in the right column:

  • its name (click to rename it; see Names and name tags) and how many visits it has made;
  • what it is doing right now;
  • its Food, Water and Rest bars;
  • a row for each trait it holds; hold Left Alt to see every scale, and hover a row for its line;
  • "Fond of" its favorite seed;
  • its last few Records;
  • Follow (the view slides along with it) and Center.

Click a feeder instead and its card shows how full it is, which seeds are in it, who is eating, and Move and Center.

Names and name tags

From the Birb Cube Wiki, in Birds
Names and name tags
Information
RenameClick the name on the bird card
TagsEsc menu, Settings

Every bird arrives with a name. Click the name on its The bird card to type a new one. Named birds can wear a floating name tag, and they drop feathers a little more often.

The Esc menu's Settings set which birds show a name tag: birds you named, all birds, or none. Lines over a bird's head also tell you when it "has entered the chat", "has rejoined the chat" (a regular coming back) or "has left the chat".

See also

Regulars

From the Birb Cube Wiki, in Birds
Regulars
Information
ReturnThe same name, look and traits

Most birds come back. A bird that leaves (for any reason but old age) may return later as a regular: the same name, look, traits, home and memories. Its card counts its visits, and it "has rejoined the chat". When a regular of a kind is away, many arrivals of that kind are that regular coming back.

Hearthbound birds and Oath-keepers come back most; Wayfarers may never return. Regulars and named birds drop feathers a little more often. Regulars remember where you fed them: see Feeding spots.

See also

  • Feeding spots
  • Traits
  • Names and name tags

Feeding spots

From the Birb Cube Wiki, in Birds
Feeding spots
Information
RememberedUp to three per bird
FadeWhen not visited

A bird that finishes a meal of seed you poured remembers the spot. It keeps up to three such spots, and they fade if it stops finding food there.

  • A returning regular flies straight to its best spot, and the log says so.
  • A hungry bird with nothing in reach may fly over to check one of its spots.
  • Seed at one of its spots counts as closer than it is, so a bird prefers it.

Feed in the same places and your regulars will learn them.

See also

  • Regulars
  • Pouring
  • Birds and your seed

Calls

From the Birb Cube Wiki, in Birds
Calls
Information
SoundsOne voice per species

Birds call every so often, and hold their call if a neighbor has just called, so the garden never sounds crowded. They sing most at dawn and less in the evening, in the rain and at night. A Town Crier calls often and won't wait its turn; a Hushed bird seldom calls.

Records
Information
KeptThe last few things a bird lived through

Each bird keeps a short record of what has happened to it, shown at the bottom of its The bird card with the day: "Froze under the Hawk's Shadow, day 4". A regular brings its record back with it.

Each species has its own looks, size, color, the seeds it eats, the Feeders it uses, the way its Traits lean, its voice, and a rarity: common, uncommon or rare. Its rarity decides which feather it drops.

Dusk DoveCommonMilletTray onlyDusk Down
GildfinchUncommonThistleTurret best, TrayGild Quill

The common and uncommon birds also pick at wild seed. You can add species of your own in the The Birb Designer: see Designer species.

Emberwing

From the Birb Cube Wiki, in Species
Emberwing
The Emberwing cock
Information
RarityCommon
LovesCorn
Also eatsWild seed
FeedersTray and Turret
FeatherEmber Plume (Common)
LooksCock and hen

A red, medium-sized bird, usually the first to find your corn. It comes as a cock or a hen. Emberwings lean bold and loud: many are Stout-hearted, Town Criers, Early Risers or Rain-proud, and few are Faint-hearted.

Dusk Dove

From the Birb Cube Wiki, in Species
Dusk Dove
A Dusk Dove
Information
RarityCommon
LovesMillet
Also eatsWild seed
FeedersTray only
FeatherDusk Down (Common)

A pale gray dove, the biggest of the built-in birds. Doves eat out of the Almoner's Tray but can't perch on the Turret Feeder. They lean shy and quiet, and many are Night Owls, so they are the birds you see most at night. Few are Stout-hearted, Early Risers or Rain-proud.

Gildfinch

From the Birb Cube Wiki, in Species
Gildfinch
A Gildfinch
Information
RarityUncommon
LovesThistle
Also eatsMillet a little, wild seed
FeedersTurret best, Tray
FeatherGild Quill (Uncommon)

A small golden-orange finch, the smallest of the built-in birds. Gildfinches love thistle and like the Turret Feeder best. They lean Dainty, Town Crier, Wayfarer and Early Riser. As an uncommon bird, a Gildfinch drops Uncommon Feathers, which buy thistle and the Turret Feeder.

Frostcrest

From the Birb Cube Wiki, in Species
Frostcrest
A Frostcrest
Information
RarityRare
LureBlue Barley
Also eatsCorn, barely
FeedersTray and Turret
FeatherRime Feather (Rare)

A rare blue bird. Until you have seen one in the cube, only Blue Barley draws it. A lured Frostcrest flies straight in. Once one has been spotted, it also comes for corn now and then.

Frostcrests lean Wayfarer, Hushed, Wary, Night Owl and Rain-proud. Once you have seen one, a Frostcrest can also mind the store's counter.

Your first Blue Barley comes from the crate by the store's door. See Lure seed.

Designer species

From the Birb Cube Wiki, in Species
Designer species
Information
Made inThe Birb Designer
Feather"<Name> Feather"

In the The Birb Designer's Species section you can make a species of your own: its name, map color, size, rarity, the seeds it likes, how its traits lean, the feeders it uses and which built-in bird's voice it borrows (at its own pitch). A new species copies its details from one you pick, then you change what you like. Each edit saves at once.

A common or uncommon Designer species gets its own share of arrivals, drawn by the seeds it likes. A rare one needs a lure seed, like the Frostcrest. Its feather is named after it, for example "Mossback Feather".

Deleting a species' file sends its birds away for good.

Feeding

From the Birb Cube Wiki, in Feeding
Feeding
Poured seed, close up

Seed brings birds. You get it to them in two ways:

  • Pour it on the ground from the seed bucket. See Pouring.
  • Pour it into a feeder. Seed in a feeder stays fresh and draws birds better.

Feeders are the main way to feed. Seed on the ground is the small extra: it spoils, faster in the rain, and fades into the dirt or comes up as a sprout.

Which birds come depends on the seed: see Seed for who eats what. The ATTRACTS list in the left column tells you which species the seed in your bucket would draw.

See also

  • Seed
  • The seed bucket
  • Pouring
  • Feeders
Feeding
Feeding · Seed · The seed bucket · Pouring · Feeders · Birds and your seed

Seed

From the Birb Cube Wiki, in Feeding
Seed
Information
KindsCorn, Millet, Thistle, Blue Barley, wild seed
Bought atThe Gilded Granary
SeedBagLoved byKeeps on the groundJarSack
CornCastellan Feed 9EmberwingsLongest2 Common Feathers8 Common Feathers
MilletPip-Mk II MilletDusk Doves, Gildfinches a littleShortest2 Common Feathers8 Common Feathers
ThistleSquire Starter MixGildfinchesMiddling2 Uncommon Feathers8 Uncommon Feathers
Blue BarleyRoyal Reserve PelletsFrostcrestsMiddling5 Rare Feathers20 Rare Feathers
Wild seedHedgerow GleaningsCommon birds pick at itMiddlingNot soldNot sold

A jar holds a little seed and a sack holds five jars' worth, for the price of four. You start with some Corn, Millet and Thistle in their bags, and no Blue Barley.

Contents
  1. Wild seed
  2. Spoiling
  3. Favorite seed

Wild seed

A little wild seed drops on its own across the land, toward the middle and never on a rock or in the water. It keeps a garden going, but slowly; your seed is what makes it busy.

Spoiling

Seed on the ground darkens and fades into the dirt after a while; millet goes quickest and corn keeps longest. Rain spoils it faster. Seed in a feeder, and on a sprout's seedheads, stays fresh. A heap that rots away sometimes comes up as a sprout.

Favorite seed

Every bird has a favorite among the seeds its species likes, shown as "Fond of" on its The bird card. A Particular bird ignores every other pile while its favorite is about.

See also

  • The seed bucket
  • The Gilded Granary
  • Sprouts
  • Frostcrest

The seed bucket

From the Birb Cube Wiki, in Feeding
The seed bucket
Information
WhereThe left column
HoldsLayers, until stirred

The left column holds your seed bags and the see-through seed bucket.

  • Click a bag to put a scoop of its seed in the bucket. Shift-click to fill the bucket from it. Right-click to put a scoop back.
  • The bags hold a limited supply. Pouring uses it up; buying jars and sacks at the The Gilded Granary adds more.
  • Seed sits in the bucket in layers, in the order it went in. Unstirred, it pours top layer first, so a feeder fills in stripes.
  • Stir blends every layer into one mix; seed added after that forms new layers on top until the next stir.
  • Empty throws out everything in the bucket; it does not go back into the bags.
  • Hover a bag to read its label. ATTRACTS lists the species the bucket's seed would draw, so you can mix for the birds you want.

See also

  • Pouring
  • Seed
  • The Gilded Granary
Feeding
Feeding · Seed · The seed bucket · Pouring · Feeders · Birds and your seed

Pouring

From the Birb Cube Wiki, in Feeding
Pouring
Information
PourHold the right mouse button

Hold the right mouse button over the garden. The bucket follows your mouse and seed pours where it hangs. A tap pours a pinch; holding pours faster. Pouring in one place grows one mound, newer seed on top of older. Dragging leaves a trail. Hold it over a feeder to fill it.

Good pours

One big, unbroken pour of seed something eats can call a bird in: a little after you let go, a bird may fly in low out of the fog toward it, often a regular who is away. Not at night, and less in the rain.

See also

  • The seed bucket

  • Birds and your seed

Feeders

From the Birb Cube Wiki, in Feeding
Feeders
An Almoner's Tray and a Turret Feeder
Information
KindsAlmoner's Tray, Turret Feeder
Bought atThe Gilded Granary

Seed in a feeder stays fresh and draws birds better than seed on the ground, so feeders are the main way to feed.

FeederPriceWho uses it
Almoner's Tray4 Common FeathersDoves eat right out of it; most birds use it
Turret Feeder6 Uncommon FeathersTwo perches on one rod; finches love it; doves can't use it

Placing a feeder

After buying one, go back to the birds and click the dirt to set it down. It can't go next to another feeder, on a rock or in the water. Click a feeder to select it; its card has Move (pick it up and click the dirt to set it down again) and Center.

Filling it

Pour seed over it: seed that falls inside is caught. A feeder holds only so much; the rest spills onto the dirt. When you fill one, a few peckish birds nearby notice and come over.

Birds and your seed

From the Birb Cube Wiki, in Feeding
Birds and your seed
Information
NoticeHungry birds nearby
MarkA sparkle, or a heart for a favorite

Birds notice when your seed lands. Hungry birds close by look toward it, then hop or fly over. Fresh seed on the ground can start a squabble: two birds face off, the bolder or bigger one wins, and the loser flies off and avoids that pile for a while.

The first bite of your seed shows a little sparkle over the bird. If it is the bird's favorite seed, a heart shows instead.

Birds also remember where they ate your seed: see Feeding spots.

See also

  • Pouring
  • Feeding spots

Feathers

From the Birb Cube Wiki, in Feathers and the store
Feathers
Information
KindsCommon, Uncommon, Rare
ShownThe right column
Spent atThe Gilded Granary

Feathers are what you pay with at the The Gilded Granary. A bird that finishes a full meal sometimes drops one of its own. It lies on the ground until it fades, sooner when it is out of view. Click it to pick it up. The log says whose it was, for example "Collected an Ember Plume (Common)".

Each feather counts by its species' rarity:

KindDropped by
Common FeatherEmberwings, Dusk Doves and common Designer species
Uncommon FeatherGildfinches and uncommon Designer species
Rare FeatherFrostcrests and rare Designer species

Rarer birds drop feathers less often. Regulars and named birds drop them a little more often, and Open-handed birds more often still.

The right column lists each kind once you have collected your first, with a count. Feathers are only for spending; they never pile up in the room.

  • The Gilded Granary
  • The ledger

The Gilded Granary

From the Birb Cube Wiki, in Feathers and the store
The Gilded Granary
The Gilded Granary by day
Information
OpenThe SHOP side of the rocker
Pays inFeathers

The Gilded Granary is a self-serve store the cube can show in place of the garden. Flip the rocker on the control deck to SHOP; flip it to BIRB to go back, or click the Zoo Cam in the right column.

Contents
  1. The shelves
  2. Feeders
  3. The counter
  4. The lure crate

The shelves

Each seed gets a section of the shelf once you hold a feather of the kind that pays for it: jars on the top boards, sacks on the bottom. Four sections fit on a page; arrows on the wall turn the page. Prices are in feathers; see Seed.

Click a jar or sack to see its price tag, with Buy and Cancel. Bought seed goes into its bag in the left column. A bought item is replaced on the shelf after a while.

Feeders

The two Feeders stand on the floor at the ends of the shelf.

The counter

A birb sits behind the counter and watches what you look at. The shopkeeper changes every few minutes. The ledger book on the counter opens the The ledger, for trading feathers.

The lure crate

The crate by the door holds a jar of a rare bird's lure seed, paid in feathers of any kind. See Lure seed.

When it is night in the garden, the store is lamp-lit.

See also

  • Feathers
  • Seed
  • Feeders
  • The ledger
  • Lure seed

The ledger

From the Birb Cube Wiki, in Feathers and the store
The ledger
The Gilded Granary lamp-lit at night
Information
WhereThe book on the store's counter
Rate3 feathers for 1 of the next kind up

Click the ledger book on the Gilded Granary's counter to trade feathers between neighboring kinds: 3 Common Feathers for 1 Uncommon, 3 Uncommon for 1 Rare, or the other way, 1 for 3. Pick a trade from the list, then press Trade. Only kinds you have already collected are offered.

When a price tag says you are short, the ledger may help.

See also

  • Feathers

Lure seed

From the Birb Cube Wiki, in Feathers and the store
Lure seed
Information
ExampleBlue Barley, for the Frostcrest
Paid inFeathers of any kind

A rare species can't be drawn by ordinary seed. Each rare species has a lure seed, and until one of its birds has been seen in the cube, only that seed draws it. The Frostcrest's lure is Blue Barley.

Since you can't have its Rare Feathers before you have met it, the store sells the lure on the crate by the door for feathers of any kind. Once you hold a Rare Feather, the lure gets a section of the shelf like any other seed, priced in Rare Feathers.

Pour the lure seed and wait. A lured bird flies straight in. Once one has been spotted, the species also comes for its other seeds.

See also

  • Frostcrest
  • The Gilded Granary
  • Seed

The Storyteller

From the Birb Cube Wiki, in Events
The Storyteller
Information
EventsBig, Gift and Small
DangerNone

Every so often something happens in the garden. The Storyteller paces these events: a quiet stretch, a small event, quiet again, a bigger one, then a guaranteed rest. Only one happens at a time.

  • Big: the Hawk's Shadow and the Murmuration.
  • Gift: the Windfall.

Events fit the moment: no hawk at night, no murmuration without seed on the ground, and a quiet garden leans toward gifts while a crowded one leans toward the big events. They never get harsher as your garden grows, and you never have to respond to one. While you watch, they tend to happen where you are looking; while you are away, they still happen and are logged.

Birds react to events by their Traits, and remember them in their Records. A short label in the cube names an event as it starts.

See also

  • The Hawk's Shadow
  • Murmuration
  • Windfall
Events
The Storyteller · The Hawk's Shadow · Murmuration · Windfall
Categories: Events

The Hawk's Shadow

From the Birb Cube Wiki, in Events
The Hawk's Shadow
The shadow crossing the garden
Information
KindBig event
NeverAt night

A hawk's shadow crosses the garden in a straight line. It is the only danger in the game, and nobody gets hurt. Each bird it comes near reacts once, by its nerve:

  • A Watchman sees it coming from farther off and calls the alarm, and after that every bird reacts from farther off.
  • Faint-hearted birds scatter into the fog, Wary ones often, average ones sometimes; the rest freeze for a while.
  • A Stout-hearted bird eating at a feeder holds its place; elsewhere it freezes only briefly.
  • Bathers burst out of the water and scatter; nappers wake up first. Sleeping Night Owls sleep through it.

Birds that scattered fly back near their homes one by one, a minute or so after the shadow has passed. Each bird that reacted gets a line in its record.

See also

  • The Storyteller
  • Traits
  • Records
Events
The Storyteller · The Hawk's Shadow · Murmuration · Windfall
Categories: Events

Murmuration

From the Birb Cube Wiki, in Events
Murmuration
A flock sweeping in for the seed
Information
KindBig event
NeedsSeed on the ground

A big flock of one common species flies in from one side, eats the seed on the ground, and leaves together a minute or so later, or as soon as its seed is gone. The more seed is lying about, the bigger the flock. The species is the one the seed on the ground draws most.

Flock birds aren't individuals: no names, no chat lines, no feathers, and they never become regulars. Garden birds that watched from close by get a line in their record.

See also

  • The Storyteller
  • Seed

Windfall

Windfall
Information
KindGift

A gust drops a few piles of seed near where you are looking: seed the birds in the garden like, never a lure seed.

The Birb Designer

From the Birb Cube Wiki, in Making birbs
The Birb Designer
The Designer, with an Emberwing on the stand
Information
OpenB, or the Esc menu

The Birb Designer takes over the cube while it is open and pauses the garden. The birb stands in the middle in daylight; drag to turn it.

  • Edit its parts: each part has a shape, size, place, turn and color. The selected part can be highlighted.
  • Preview: test poses (hop, walk, peck, sip, bathe and more) and a zoom.
  • Save and load designs. Every saved design becomes one more look for its species: new birds of that species pick a look at random.
  • Release into the Cube saves the design and sends one bird wearing it into the middle of the view.
  • Species: pick which species the design belongs to, or make a new one. See Designer species.
  • Recipes: a gallery of birbs made from a kit of parts. See Recipe birbs.

Give eye parts the Eye role so they blink.

See also

  • Designer species
  • Recipe birbs
Making birbs
The Birb Designer · Recipe birbs
Categories: Making birbs | Interface

Recipe birbs

From the Birb Cube Wiki, in Making birbs
Recipe birbs
The Gildfinch, built from a kit of shaped parts
Information
WhereThe Designer's Recipes section
StatusDrafts, gallery only

A recipe is a whole species written as a short list of choices from a kit of parts: one option each for the body, head, neck, beak, crest, wings, tail and legs, plus markings and colors, and optional variants such as a hen. The kit fits every option to every other, so any recipe makes a sound birb.

The Designer's Recipes section opens a gallery: a wall of every recipe birb, or one recipe with every option of one part. The recipes in the game are drafts for now, shown only in the gallery: Bramble Jay, Cinder Wren, Goldplume, Mallow Teal, Mossthrush, Reedstilt, Sootcap, Swiftling and Thornshrike.
